claims.text: The baseline HEA is produced by arc melting, homogenization, and thermomechanical processing.
The baseline processing produces a uniform, single-phase microstructure.
Approximately 1–2 vol.% nano-oxide particles such as Y2O3 will be introduced into the HEA.
The oxide dispersion will be introduced through ball milling with an oxide precursor, consolidation, and heat treatment.
The intervention will produce a uniform dispersion of nano-oxide particles.
The nano-oxide dispersion can refine the HEA grain structure.
Impeded dislocation motion and restricted grain-boundary sliding retard creep deformation.
The oxide-dispersed HEA will have better creep resistance than the same HEA without oxide dispersoids.
The oxide-dispersed HEA will have greater elevated-temperature yield strength than the same HEA without oxide dispersoids.
The predicted improvements should hold between approximately 800°C and 1000°C in an inert or controlled atmosphere.
Performance outside 800–1000°C or under cyclic loading is uncertain.
Extension of the benefits above 1000°C, during rapid thermal cycling, or under fatigue loading is uncertain.
Failure to achieve a statistically significant improvement of at least 15% in creep life or yield strength at 900°C relative to the control will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial baseline is described as arc-melted, whereas the intervention uses powder metallurgy; elsewhere the control and intervention are said to be processed or consolidated identically. It is therefore unclear whether the baseline is arc-melted or is a powder-metallurgy control without oxide.

The proposed creep test is described as using a constant strain rate, while creep life and time to rupture are described as measured under constant load. These are different loading protocols and cannot simultaneously define the same test without further clarification.
